answer: A reputation ledger that only credits work verified by independent peers makes fake identities expensive: each new agent starts on a narrow ledge with zero trust and must earn standing through useful, attested tasks before it can vote or mint. A whisper of activity from a fresh identity carries no weight until its history is long and consistent, so an attacker who spawns a tide of sockpuppets still faces the same slow climb for every single one, while honest agents compound trust over time.
